summary: Energy led commodity gains again in the week to Friday 21 August 2026. WTI settled near 87.06 USD/Bbl, up 0.26% on the day and about 5.7% on the week, a second straight weekly advance, as Strait of Hormuz tanker flows slowed to an estimated 2.0 million b/d from roughly 4.0 million b/d in July and Washington shifted from military action to sweeping new sanctions on Iran. Diesel crack spreads topped 100 USD/Bbl, a record, on constrained refining capacity. Henry Hub gas was little changed at 2.77 USD/MMBtu after a smaller-than-forecast 16 Bcf storage injection. Base metals firmed, with copper up 1.85% on the day, aluminum 1.92% and zinc 1.99%, though copper ended slightly lower on the week. Precious metals rallied hardest: gold broke above 4,600 USD/oz for a third consecutive weekly gain of roughly 5% and silver held above 69 USD/oz after the US Treasury unexpectedly expanded long-dated bond buybacks, pushing the dollar below 99. MP Materials, used here as a rare earths proxy, closed up 9.10% at 60.05 USD/share after a Morgan Stanley target lift extended a post-Q2 rally. Next week brings US core PCE, Q2 GDP revisions and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech.
